approach: Two linked changes, both using the one classifier `athena_core::disk::is_environment_reason` / `resumable_stop`. (1) drain.rs: an attempt whose run reason, or whose reader error, is an environment stop ends the item with a new non-failure `ItemEnd::Environment(job)`. It is returned before `failures += 1`. The drain adds the item's last job to `tried` so the re-read queue cannot hand it back in the same run, and the next item runs. (2) steward.rs: `interrupted_work` also lists drained-channel jobs closed Failed with an environment reason (via `disk::resumable_stop`, no new list) that no later "try again on" request retries. A later drain therefore retries them through `ReadOf::Retry`, and "stays queued for a later run" is true in the records, not only in the report. `repeated_failures` skips environment-stop jobs. Landing failures are checked and left alone, with the reason recorded. display.rs needs no change.

decisions.choice: Classify with `athena_core::disk::is_environment_reason` on `run.reason` in `run_job`, and on the reader's error text on the read path. No list is added to athena-cli.
decisions.reason: disk.rs is documented as the one place that says which closing reasons are environment stops. It also handles the older unprefixed 'the producer did not complete: ... 401' form. A new kind of stop is added there once and the drain follows.

rejected.why: A second list. The request forbids it, and it would miss the unprefixed 401 form.

rejected.option: Add a field to `Run` or change the `Steps` trait
rejected.why: Touches every stub in tests/drain.rs. The reason is already in `Run.reason` and `Read.error`.

decisions.choice: On an environment stop the item ends for this run (`ItemEnd::Environment(job)`). It is not retried in the same run and is passed over like Held.
decisions.reason: An immediate retry hits the same expired login or full disk, spends budget, and was the second 'failure'. The request says a later run.

rejected.option: Skip the count but retry in the same run
rejected.why: Retries into the same fault and burns budget.

rejected.option: Stop the whole drain on an environment stop
rejected.why: The request says the run goes on to the next item.

decisions.choice: Make 'stays queued for a later run' true by extending `steward::interrupted_work` with `disk::resumable_stop(j.state(), reason)`. It keeps the existing drained-channel, not-running and not-already-retried filters. Add a doc line in drain.rs.
decisions.reason: The drain builds items from approved_work, queued_work and interrupted_work. queued_work needs state Queued or Proposed. A job with an outcome record is Closed(Failed) (store.rs `state()`), so neither lists it today. `resumable_stop` already says which closed-failed jobs are resumable, and Dispatched, the case interrupted_work covers today, already returns true. The change reuses it, and a retried job is excluded by the existing `retried` set, so a-retry is listed once and `a` is not. The queue item has `interrupted: true`, so its first attempt is `athena retry`, which can resume from a kept candidate.

rejected.option: Narrow the docs and CHANGELOG to 'not counted' and say the job is closed
rejected.why: The request says the item stays queued for a later run. Closed with no path back would drop work silently.

rejected.option: A new record or marker file for 'environment-stopped' items
rejected.why: The records already hold the outcome reason. Brief and assumptions say no new record or data file.

rejected.option: Add a new function next to interrupted_work
rejected.why: The drain's `queue()` would merge two lists and every caller needs both. One predicate change in the existing function is smaller.

decisions.choice: Insert the environment-stopped job into `State.tried` in `finish`. `ItemEnd::Environment(job)` carries the job the attempt last touched.
decisions.reason: The drain re-reads the queue after every wave (the `steps.queue()` call after `run(d, ...)`). With the persistent-queue change, a-retry now appears as a new item id and would be retried in the same run, again and again until the job limit. `tried` is what ends that loop.

rejected.why: It only de-duplicates a log line; `batches_for` filters on `tried`.

decisions.choice: Landing: leave `LandStep::NotLanded` counting as a failure. Record why in the report and the docs.
decisions.reason: The job there has already passed and its text comes from the host or the PR report (`landing_from_report`, `recheck_after_rebase`), not from a closing reason. It never starts with 'environment:', so the shared classifier would never match it. Matching network words would be a second list. The existing test a_job_that_does_not_land_twice_still_ends_as_repeated_failure_when_the_config_is_readable keeps the behaviour.

rejected.why: Dead code: no landing text carries the prefix.

decisions.choice: Change `steward::repeated_failures` to skip jobs whose outcome reason is an environment stop. Leave display.rs unchanged.
decisions.reason: The count is a model input signal 'repeated failure'. Counting a login-expired job there is the same fault. display.rs only formats `Stop::RepeatedFailure` after the stop is set, and no new variant exists.

rejected.option: Only record why steward.rs is unchanged
rejected.why: Leaves the same mislabel in the steward's input; the change is one extra check against the same classifier.
Notes and pass-over lines already show the reason. There is nothing new to format.

rejected.why: That was the duplicated wording the review flagged.

risks.risk: A persistent fault (an expired login) makes the drain walk the whole queue and fail each item once per run.
risks.mitigation: Each item gets one attempt per run and is not retried in it. The job limit and the budget bound the run, and the guard in `run_job` stops further starts. The docs say so.

risks.risk: The same-run requeue loop: the re-read queue lists the closed job (a-retry) as a new item.
risks.mitigation: `finish` inserts the job into `tried`, and the drain test's `queue()` re-lists it and asserts one run.

risks.risk: A work failure taken for an environment stop (the classifier accepts any 'environment:' prefix).
risks.mitigation: The classifier is applied only to the reason of a run that did not pass and was not needs-accepting or held. The existing tests with 'ended rejected' and 'checks failed' still expect RepeatedFailure.

risks.risk: The `interrupted_work` change widens what the drain picks up (see open question 2).
risks.mitigation: It uses only `resumable_stop`, the same predicate `athena retry` uses. Dispatched jobs already behave this way. Steward tests pin the listed and unlisted cases. If a reviewer rejects it, the drain-side change stands on its own with the docs narrowed.

risks.risk: The new `Stub` field breaks the many tests that build `Stub`.
risks.mitigation: `Stub` derives Default and the field defaults to empty; tests with their own `Steps` impls are untouched.

risks.risk: Adding match arms for the two new variants breaks the build elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Grep for `ItemEnd::` and `RunStep::` in drain.rs; `finish` and `attempts` are the only matches (lines ~2358-2399 and ~1746-1779).

demonstrations.method: Drive the real drain loop over a scripted world. Items a and b; outcomes [Rejected, Landed x7]; `environment_stopped: ["a-retry"]`. The stub run for a-retry returns `Run{outcome: Some(Failed), reason: format!("{PRODUCER_AUTH}: 401"), cost 0.5}` without consuming `outcomes`. Assertions: `report.stop != Stop::RepeatedFailure` and `report.failed_item.is_none()`. The log holds `run a`, `reread a`, `run a-retry` exactly once, no `reread a-retry`, then `read b`, `run b`, `land b`. `report.landed == 1`. A note contains `left queued for a later run` and the PRODUCER_AUTH text. The a-retry job line carries the reason. Two sibling tests: (i) the stop on the first attempt of a (item a ends, b still runs); (ii) the stub `read` of the retry returns `error: Some(PRODUCER_AUTH...)`, same expectations. The earlier `report.queued holds a` check is dropped because it also passes with the bug; the distinguishing checks are the stop, failed_item, the log and the note.
demonstrations.observes: The run does not end as repeated failure and goes on to b, which it lands. a-retry is run once in this run (no second attempt and no same-run requeue), and the report says it is left queued for a later run. The first-attempt and reader-error variants pass the same way.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the Environment step, the second attempt counts as failure 2, `ItemEnd::Failed` sets `Stop::RepeatedFailure` naming a, and the stop assertion fails along with `read b` / `run b` / `land b` missing from the log. Without the `tried` insert, the stub's requeued a-retry is run a second time and the 'exactly one run a-retry' assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_cli::drain::drain(&stub, limits(5.0), &Quiet)`. Its guards are `stop_requested`, the budget, `paused` and the job limit. The fake is `Stub`, which implements `Steps` in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs and is passed as the first argument. It exists today. Step 5 adds one field, `environment_stopped: Vec<&'static str>`, and a `Stub::run` branch that only scripts the reason. The same field makes `Stub::queue` list a job once its `run` is in the log, as an `interrupted: true` item, which stands in for the real queue listing the closed job. The classification, the item end and the `tried` handling under test stay in drain.rs.

demonstrations.method: Steward tests in `mod tests` of steward.rs on `Records::default()` filled with `JobRecords{id, request: Some(Request{channel, text, received_at,..}), outcome: Some(Outcome{state, reason,..})}`. (a) `repeated_failures`: one Rejected plus one Failed with reason PRODUCER_AUTH in one class_of_work gives an empty map; one Rejected plus one Failed with 'checks failed' gives one group of two. (b) `interrupted_work`: a 'cli' job closed Failed with PRODUCER_AUTH is listed; the same with 'checks failed' is not; a Rejected job is not; a job closed Failed with PRODUCER_AUTH that a later request 'try again on <id>' retries is not listed (the retry itself, if it also failed for the environment, is); a job on another channel is not listed; the existing Dispatched case still is. It also states the landing and reader-path findings.

open_questions: Do the real reader errors carry the 'environment:' prefix or the 401 form? `producer_stop_reason` is called only in run/producer.rs (line 208), and I did not read the reader's error text. The reader-path check is therefore correct but may rarely fire; the drain test uses a scripted error. If real reader errors never match, a follow-up should route them through `producer_stop_reason` (in athena-core, outside this change).

Backlog on first use: jobs closed Failed with an environment reason before this change, on the 'cli' or 'steward' channel and not retried, become drain work. 'cli' is also the channel of plain `athena ask`, and there is no way to dismiss a closed job. Drain limits, budget and the scope-guard pause bound the effect. The producer should keep the rule as stated; a human should decide whether an age limit is wanted.

'Network' has no cause of its own in `StopCause`; only reasons with the 'environment:' prefix, low disk, a check timeout and the 401/429 forms count. Changing the classifier is out of scope, so a network stop is covered only when its closing reason carries the prefix.

Whether the real `Steps::run` returns the closing reason of an environment-stopped job in `Run.reason`: drain.rs:1515 sets `line.reason` from it, and `go_with_stages` returns `f.reason` from the finished outcome, but I did not read the producer-stop path end to end.
